newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN DOLLAR REBOUNDS FROM 9-YEAR BRINK AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN DOLLAR REBOUNDS FROM 9-YEAR BRINK AT CLOSE.

text.p: Strong intervention orchestrated by the central bank in the final seconds of Thursday's trade reeled the Taiwan dollar back from the brink of another nine-year low close, ensuring a slightly firmer finish, dealers said.
The local dollar once tumbled to as low as T$28.970 in brisk late trade before rebounding sharply as the clock ran out to close at T$28.639 against Wednesday's T$28.656 finish.
Turnover through dealers was extremely hectic at US$572 million -- some US$186 million of it in the final minutes.
With greenback buying heavy throughout much of the session, some dealers had predicted the central bank to step in and intervene in defence of the local dollar.
"U.S. dollar buying is very heavy, but I don't think the central bank will allow such a sharp depreciation," one dealer said just before the final flurry of greenback selling.
"There is still one minute left, let's wait and see."
Sure enough, the sagging rate promptly rose -- a dramatic reverse that dealers said had all the earmarks of intervention.
Dealers said the central bank's dramatic move was a clear attempt to rein in offshore speculators, who had been buying U.S. dollars in the form of non-delivery forward trading.
"It's obvious that the central bank was punishing those offshore speculators -- they were perceived as the abnormal factors by the central bank," the dealer said.
"The central bank had repeatedly said it would intervene when abnormal factors occur. Its determination is unquestionable," the dealer said.

The central bank raised two key interest rates on July 31, saying it was necessary to stabilise the foreign exchange market -- though analysts said they suspected the bank also wanted to cool the red-hot stock market's huge recent turnover.
The bank has said a southeast Asia-style currency crisis could not happen in Taiwan because the government can marshal appropriate defences.
Dealers said the central bank would continue to smooth, if not halt, the currency's fall amid strong greenback demand.
"I think the market has learned its lession. It will definitely behave tomorrow," the dealer said.
A range of T$28.60-80 was seen for Friday.
